verses.deuteronomy/11/14: וְנָתַתִּ֥י מְטַֽר־אַרְצְכֶ֛ם בְּעִתּ֖וֹ יוֹרֶ֣ה וּמַלְק֑וֹשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ֣ דְגָנֶ֔ךָ וְתִירֹשְׁךָ֖ וְיִצְהָרֶֽךָ:

verses.deuteronomy/11/16: הִשָּֽׁמְר֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם פֶּ֥ן־יִפְתֶּ֖ה לְבַבְכֶ֑ם וְסַרְתֶּ֗ם וַֽעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם:

decisions.evidence: maariv-s20-mezuzot.png shows the letters מ ז ז ו ת. There is a shva under מ and a qubbutz (three slanted dots) under the first ז. No vav comes between the two zayins. A slanted stroke under the second ז reads as merkha. The only vav is the one after the second ז, and it carries a holam dot. So the first vowel is defective and the second is plene, the reverse of WLC מְזוּזֹת. maariv-s20-shema.png agrees.

maariv-s22-taturoo.png shows the letters ת ת ו ר ו. There is a qamatz under the first ת. A slanted stroke above the second ת reads as geresh. Nothing is printed under the second ת, so there is no qubbutz. A vav carrying a dot follows it, read as shureq, so the word is plene, not WLC תָתֻ֜רוּ. וְלֹא has a shva under ו and a holam on ל, with no meteg visible under ל. A space follows it, not a maqaf.

maariv-s22-rubrics.png has enough room below the line to show the pointing that was cut off before. יהוה has a shva under י and a qamatz under ו, with no holam, and a slanted mark below read as merkha. אלהיכם has a hataf segol under א, a holam on ל, a tsere under ה, a segol plus a vertical stroke (silluq) under כ, and a two-dot colon after it.
maariv-s18-shema.png shows a small isolated mark between the two words. The ד is enlarged.
The space is only the page turn from s18 to s20. The maqaf is printed at the end of s18.
maariv-s20-middle.png shows a horizontal stroke at the top of the line between the words. WLC, which prints a space, is not followed.

decisions.accepted: plene holam-vav in the first syllable
decisions.evidence: maariv-s20-middle.png shows a vav after the first ט. Compare לְטֹטָפֹ֖ת at 6:8 in s20-shema, which has no vav.
A holam dot is printed above the vav. WLC's U+05BA (holam haser for vav) versus U+05B9 is an encoding choice and not a difference in the print.

decisions.accepted: a short mark next to the patach under ו, encoded as meteg
decisions.evidence: A small stroke sits beside the patach in s20-middle, s20-numbers and s22-shema. Its exact shape (meteg or munach) is only moderately clear at this resolution.

decisions.accepted: יש לצרף אלהיכם לאמת, אכן יתן רוח מעט שלא יבולע הא׳.
decisions.evidence: From maariv-s22-rubrics.png. The second word has the same Rashi tsadi-resh-pe shape as elsewhere, so it is לצרף, not [לסמוך]. The first letter of אכן matches the Rashi alef in אלהיכם and לאמת, so it is not lamed (לכן). The noun has three letters, resh-vav-het: there is no yod, so it is not ריוח, and the first letter matches the resh in לצרף, not a kaf (כוח). The verb has a vav after the ב, so it is יבולע, not יבלע. The abbreviation is הא׳ and the line ends with a period.
